expectations_used.communicate: Keeps a running account while reading roster.py, policy.py and router.py, saying which candidate explanation each observation rules out — skill match, concurrency cap, tenure bar, rank ordering — and announcing each move from the failing test to the filter to the ranking rather than working silently.
expectations_used.implement: Corrects the boundary in minutes_into_shift so an agent stops being eligible at their shift end minute, matching the half-open Shift.covers, and leaves the rank key, the tenure bar and the tests untouched.

summary: The candidate spent almost the entire six-minute session re-running the same failing test suite without opening any source files, only voicing a correct-sounding hypothesis about an inclusive-vs-half-open shift boundary in the final seconds after two interviewer nudges, then ended the session before writing any fix or verifying it.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate never asked a clarifying question about what the failing test expects; they mostly re-ran the same suite repeatedly without opening the failing test file or the relevant source files. Even after the interviewer pointed out the oren-vs-nadia failure directly, they did not probe further into what minute boundary was in dispute before landing on an answer.

Near the very end, only after a direct nudge from the interviewer, the candidate did articulate a specific and largely correct mechanism -- that the on-shift boundary check is inclusive where the model is half-open, letting the outgoing agent survive at the handover minute. This is the right mechanism, but it came very late and only as a response to repeated prompting rather than from their own investigation of the code.

For most of the six minutes the candidate said almost nothing while repeatedly running the same failing test suite; there is no narration of what they were reading or ruling out. The single substantive statement of their hypothesis comes at the very end, following a second nudge, so the transcript does not explain their path leading up to it.

The candidate never opened or edited any source file (policy.py, router.py, roster.py) during the session -- all actions were repeated test runs -- so there is nothing to assess about whether execution matched a stated plan.
No code fix was ever made, so there is nothing to verify; the repeated test runs prior to any hypothesis or edit do not constitute verification of a fix.

The session ended immediately after the candidate stated their hypothesis, with no code change and no discussion of why it would fix the defect versus merely making the assertion pass, so there is no reflection to assess.
